How analysis is planned, produced, assured and communicated at NHSBSA. It covers every analytical
output, whether it is published, used for an internal decision, or given to a sponsor.

## The short path

::: {.callout-important title="Most analysis needs nothing but this" appearance="minimal" icon=false}
<br>
**1. [Agree the question](guidance/01-engagement-and-scoping/index.qmd).**
With your commissioner: the decision the analysis supports, the question in one sentence, what is
out of scope, and the deadline. The level is scored from this, so it comes first.

**2. [Decide your assurance level](guidance/07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd).** Score six
impact dimensions and six likelihood dimensions with your commissioner, take the highest of each,
and read your level off the matrix. About five minutes, still at scoping and before the design is
settled.

**3. [Do what that level requires](guidance/07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd).** Read the column for your
level. The levels are cumulative, so yours does everything the levels below it do and adds its own.

That is the whole path for most analysis. Everything below exists for when you need it.
:::

## Where you are in the work

The analytical lifecycle is the shape of the work and the shape of this playbook. Five phases and a
loop back. The analytical lifecycle band of the sidebar opens on a picture of the whole cycle and
then runs the guidance in the order the work happens, naming the phase each page belongs to. The
other bands hold the rest: the routes in, the four roles, the pages for a particular job, and the
resources.

```{=html}
<ol class="pb-phases">
  <li>
    <h3><a href="guidance/01-engagement-and-scoping/index.html">Phase 1. Engagement and scoping</a></h3>
    <p>Agree the question and the decision it supports, then score the assurance level from it.
    Business Critical is settled here too. Most of what goes wrong later was decided here.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <h3><a href="guidance/02-design/index.html">Phase 2. Design</a></h3>
    <p>Choose the method, plan the assurance the level requires, and name your critical friend
    before the work starts rather than after it.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <h3><a href="guidance/03-analysis/index.html">Phase 3. Analysis</a></h3>
    <p>Do the work and the checks together. Record assumptions and limitations as you meet them,
    not from memory at the end.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <h3><a href="guidance/04-delivery-and-sign-off/index.html">Phase 4. Delivery and sign-off</a></h3>
    <p>Write the quality assurance statement, carry the caveats with the numbers, and get the
    approval the level requires.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <h3><a href="guidance/05-review/index.html">Phase 5. Review</a></h3>
    <p>Ask whether the analysis worked and whether it is still right. What this phase finds is
    what Phase 1 of the next piece of work starts from.</p>
  </li>
</ol>
```

**Producing analysis and assuring it are different jobs.** The phases above are what the analyst
does. The assurance that runs alongside them is
[deciding your assurance level](guidance/07-deciding-your-assurance-level/index.qmd), and who may do it is
[roles and responsibilities](guidance/06-roles/index.qmd): the assurer and the analyst shall be
independent, and how far apart follows the level. You hold one of those roles on one piece of work.

## Find your role

```{=html}
<ul class="pb-cards">
  <li>
    <h3><a href="guidance/06-roles/analyst.html">Analyst: plan it, do it, document it</a></h3>
    <p>You own the method, your own checks and the write-up. Nine stops, from the question to the
    lesson that reaches the next piece of work.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <h3><a href="guidance/06-roles/commissioner.html">Commissioner: state the decision and the deadline</a></h3>
    <p>You own the question the analysis answers, the assurance level agreed with the analyst, and
    the time and resource to deliver it.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <h3><a href="guidance/06-roles/critical-friend.html">Critical friend: give independent advice</a></h3>
    <p>You review one assignment. You and the analyst shall be separate in all cases, and how far
    apart follows the level.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <h3><a href="guidance/06-roles/analysis-senior-responsible-officer.html">Analysis Senior Responsible Officer: approve it as fit for use</a></h3>
    <p>You are named at scoping for Business Critical work, and you approve the output after
    reviewing the assurance evidence.</p>
  </li>
  <li>
    <h3><a href="guidance/09-resources/r3-who-to-ask.html">Somebody else, or not sure yet</a></h3>
    <p>Who to ask for a level dispute, a critical friend, advice on official statistics,
    information governance, or help with analytical code.</p>
  </li>
</ul>
```

## This playbook is based on

- [Government Functional Standard GovS 010: Analysis](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-analysis-functional-standard--2/government-functional-standard-govs-010-analysis)
- [The AQuA Book: guidance on producing quality analysis for government](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/the-aqua-book)
- [The Code of Practice for Statistics](https://osr.statisticsauthority.gov.uk/the-code-of-practice-for-statistics/)

The [Green Book](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-green-book-appraisal-and-evaluation-in-central-government)
and [Magenta Book](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-magenta-book) also cover analysis
involving appraisal and evaluation.
